findings.description: The status line is read with getline(st,reason) and re-emitted as HTTP/1.1 <code><reason>. A reason containing a bare CR and then header text lands those bytes before the proxy's own header block. An upstream reason of OK\rContent-Length: 999 yields a client head with a rogue Content-Length: 999 ahead of the real Content-Length: 5; with OK\rSet-Cookie: a=b two live cookies are installed. CRLF-strict clients take the first CL and starve, CR-splitting clients see three headers. Precondition: an attacker-influenced upstream.
findings.title: The upstream reason phrase is copied verbatim into the client head, so a bare CR in it pre-empts headers the proxy writes

findings.description: The bodyless branch still appends Content-Length if the upstream supplied a length and the code is not 204. A 304 with Content-Length: 5 was forwarded with that CL even though no body follows, so a client that honours CL on a bodyless status waits. Precondition: an upstream that sends CL on a bodyless status.
findings.title: Content-Length is emitted on a 204, a bodyless status, when the upstream sent one
